summary: At the December 2, 2025 Allen Township Trustees regular session, attorney Cindy Land briefed the Trustees on a legal action filed by One Power Company against the Hancock County Board of Elections concerning the Allen Township Zoning Resolution ballot language. Judge Jonathan P. Starn issued a Decision and Order (Case No. 2025 CV 00168) finding the Board of Elections failed to meet obligations under R.C. 3505.06(E), rendering the May 6, 2025 Primary Election results on the Proposed Allen Township Zoning Plan invalid and void, thereby returning Allen Township to unzoned status. The Board of Elections has filed an appeal and a stay, and the matter is ordered to be placed on the May 5, 2026 Primary Election Ballot with compliant summary language. All zoning certificates issued July through October 2025 were declared unwarranted and associated fees are being returned.
corridor_relevance: The meeting connects to the subject "one_power" because One Power Company is named as the plaintiff in a complaint (Case No. 2025 CV 00168) filed on May 1, 2025 against the Hancock County Board of Elections challenging the ballot language for the Allen Township Zoning Resolution; the minutes do not describe One Power Company's nature, purpose, or any project beyond its role as the filing party in that legal action.

summary: At the March 26, 2026 Hancock County Commissioners meeting, Deb Stacy raised concerns about the county commissioners' and township trustees' limited role in economic development, which led to a broader discussion about annexations, utilities, and data centers. Commissioner Bechtol clarified that there is no state statute permitting county commissioners to enact a county-wide moratorium on data centers, noting this is a zoning function. Discussion also touched on the ability of townships, villages, and the City of Findlay to implement their own moratoriums on data centers, as well as an Economic Development study on the subject.
